Now: %1$s
Recommendations
The first days. Cravings and irritability are strongest, and your brain expects the old routine.
Remove objects and apps linked to the habit from sight.
Get through the next 24 hours; you do not have to solve everything at once.
Replace the ritual with a short action: water, a walk, breathing, a shower.
Physical cravings weaken, but your brain still offers the old script.
Notice the “I really want it” moment and wait 10 minutes.
Make triggers inconvenient: remove, block, change your route.
Replace the same ritual at the same time and place.
The new way is becoming more familiar, but stress can bring the old one back.
Decide in advance what to do with stress, boredom, and company.
Do not test whether it will work — keep going mechanically.
Keep sleep, movement, and food as your base.
It is getting easier. This is exactly when overconfidence is dangerous.
Do not bring old triggers back “just to test”.
Keep a plan for a slip.
Notice the changes, but do not turn them into permission to return.
90 days without a slip is an important milestone. The habit no longer runs you automatically, but the old pattern can return. Life goes on — keep maintaining.
Keep the new rituals and environment.
Plan difficult situations in advance.
After day 90, keep maintaining: a slip is an event, not a return to the start.

Days %1$d–%2$d
Now
The final stretch
Almost there. The new pattern is working, but this is exactly when it is easy to relax too early.
Do not bring old triggers back “just to test”.
Plan difficult situations in advance.
Keep the new rituals until day 90, not earlier.
After day 90
You have come a long way. Now you have control over yourself.
